entries.title: 🌳 Branching - Alternate Realities
entries.content:
Think of the `main` branch as your 'clean' code. NEVER work directly on main if you're trying something risky.

- Creating a Branch - `git checkout -b feature-name` (This creates a new timeline and jumps into it).
- Switching Back - `git checkout main` (Teleport back to reality).
- Why do it? - If you break everything in your `feature` branch, your `main` branch stays safe and working.
tips: Type `git branch` to see where you are so you don't get lost in the multiverse.

entries.title: 🤝 Merging & PRs - The Fusion
entries.content:
Once your code in a branch is perfect, you need to bring it back to the main project.

- Merging - You go to `main` and say `git merge feature-name`. It sucks all the code from the branch into the main timeline.
- Pull Requests (PRs) - This is the 'Social' version of a merge. On GitHub/GitLab, you ask: 'Hey, can I merge this?' and people can comment on it before it happens.
- Merge Conflicts - The 'Boss Fight' of Git. Happens when you and a friend (or the AI) edited the same line. You just have to pick which version you want to keep manually.
tips: Always pull before you push! `git pull origin main` keeps your local code up to date.
PRs are great for 'Peer Learning' - ask a friend to review your code before merging.

entries.title: 🆘 The 'Oh Shit' Kit
entries.content:
If you feel lost, these three commands are your flashlight in the dark:

- `git status` - Tells you what files are changed and what branch you're on. Run this EVERY 5 MINUTES.
- `git log --oneline` - Shows you a neat list of your past 'save points'.
- `git checkout -- file` - The 'Ctrl+Z' for files. It throws away your changes and resets the file to the last commit.
tips: Commit often, but only when the code compiles. Nobody likes a 'Save Game' that starts inside a wall.
If you get stuck in a weird text editor after committing, try typing `:wq` and press Enter to escape.
